properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It came from the dev_reflow2 two-agent exercise, 2026-09-28/29 (art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, items D16 and I22). The owner kept flo2's existing gateway, so the new engine's "gateway" part became its "router". The designer deleted and re-created it and lost its history. Designer's words: "Expected: a rename or id-move that keeps the edges and history." Anthony asked for every idea from the report to be brainstormed (2026-09-29).

MEASURED 2026-09-29 (the finding beside this node): no served tool moves an id. The heal merge keeps the alphabetically smaller id ("the alphabet chose the victim"), so it cannot be used as a rename. Lineage is kept per item, keyed by id.

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) A RE-KEY TOOL (`move_id`): rewrite the key, re-point every edge, carry the lineage chain across (the new node's first version names the old one's last hash), keep the old id resolvable as an alias so get_node on it answers with the new node and says so, and record a ChangeEvent. The real fix. Counter:
  - prose citations of the old id stay text;
  - the committed export churns;
  - a mirror in another design that pinned the old id breaks unless the alias travels in the export.
(b) SEPARATE KEY FROM SLUG: opaque stable keys, with the slug as a display field. Counter: a migration of every design, and the slug is load-bearing ("the id prefix names the type", and what agents search and cite).
(c) A STEERABLE MERGE: an asserted DUPLICATES with a stated direction chooses the survivor, so old merges INTO new. It reuses existing machinery. Counter: merge semantics discard the removed node's properties and delete it, so the history still goes. It is a merge, not a rename.
(d) NOTHING: keep the id and revise the name, since a key is not a claim. Counter: measured cost. The id then asserts a meaning the owner withdrew in every edge echo, citation and search hit.

RANKING, as a finding: (d) costs nothing and is wrong in public; (c) is cheap and loses history; (a) is the correct one and must decide how an alias travels in the export; (b) is the largest change and the least likely to pay back.
properties.name: OPEN — when what a node MEANS changes, can it be re-keyed (cmp:gateway → cmp:router) and keep its edges, its lineage and a resolvable old id, instead of either keeping an id that now says the wrong thing or deleting its history?
properties.rationale: One measured instance so far (the ikg designer). Recorded because the report's conclusion was confirmed, not overturned: there is no route today that keeps both the meaning and the history.
